matrix.rule: "Backer" means any individual with a direct or indirect financial interest in a cannabis establishment. "Backer" does not include an individual with an investment interest in a cannabis establishment if (A) the interest held by such individual and such individual's spouse, parent or child, in the aggregate, does not exceed five per cent of the total ownership or interest rights in such cannabis establishment, and (B) such individual does not participate directly or indirectly in the control, management or operation of the cannabis establishment
matrix.notes: Two cumulative conditions for the 5% carve-out: BOTH the size test and the no-control test must be met. An individual under 5% who participates in control is still a backer.

matrix.rule: "Equity joint venture" means a business entity that is controlled, and at least fifty percent owned, by an individual or individuals, or such applicant is an individual, who meets the criteria of subparagraphs (A) and (B) of subdivision (51) of this section
matrix.notes: Two limbs: CONTROL and at least 50% OWNERSHIP. Ownership alone does not satisfy it. Subdivision numbering moved: earlier text cross-refers to 21a-420(48)(A) and (B).

matrix.rule: "Social equity applicant" means a person that has applied for a license for a cannabis establishment, where such applicant is controlled, and at least sixty-five percent owned, by an individual or individuals, or such applicant is an individual, who: (A) Had an average household income of less than three hundred percent of the state median household income over the three tax years immediately preceding such individual's application; and (B)(i) Was a resident of a disproportionately impacted area for not less than five of the ten years immediately preceding the date of such application; or (ii) Was a resident of a disproportionately impacted area for not less than nine years prior to attaining the age of eighteen
matrix.notes: 65% for a social equity applicant; 50% for an equity joint venture. Different tests. RENUMBERED: P.A. 26-8 moved this definition from subdivision (51) to subdivision (54) of CGS 21a-420. Cross-references in 21a-420u(b), 21a-420j(b), 21a-420m(b) and 21a-420d(k) were conformed effective 1 October 2026.

matrix.rule: From July 1, 2021, until June 30, 2025, the department shall not award a cannabis establishment license to any lottery applicant who, at the time the lottery is conducted, has two or more licenses or includes a backer that has managerial control of, or is a backer of, two or more licensees in the same license type or category for which the applicant has entered the lottery, provided an ownership interest in an equity joint venture or a social equity partner in accordance with subsection (c) of section 21a-420l shall not be considered for purposes of such cap. For purposes of this section, dispensary facility, retailer and hybrid retailer licenses shall be considered to be within the same license category and producer, cultivator and micro-cultivator licenses shall be considered to be within the same license category.
matrix.notes: EXPIRED. Applies only to LOTTERY applicants, only in that window, and EXPRESSLY EXCLUDES equity joint venture interests from the count. Must not be applied to 2026 conduct or to non-lottery licensing.

matrix.rule: A cultivator licensed under section 21a-420o may create not more than two equity joint ventures to be approved by the Social Equity Council under section 21a-420d, and licensed by the department under this section. The equity joint venture shall be in any cannabis establishment licensed business, other than a cultivator license.
matrix.notes: Two per cultivator.

matrix.rule: A cultivator licensed under section 21a-420o, including the backer of such cultivator, shall not increase its ownership in an equity joint venture in excess of fifty per cent during the seven-year period after a license is issued by the department under this section.
matrix.notes: Runs from the DEPARTMENT license issue date, not from formation or SEC approval.

matrix.rule: Equity joint ventures that are retailers or hybrid retailers that share a common cultivator backer or owner shall not be located within twenty miles of each other.
matrix.notes: Not retroactive. The statute does not state how distance is measured.

matrix.rule: In order for a dispensary facility to convert its license to a hybrid-retailer license, a dispensary facility shall have a workforce development plan that has been approved by the Social Equity Council under section 21a-420d and shall either pay the fee of one million dollars established in section 21a-420e or, if such dispensary facility has committed to create one equity joint venture ... pay a reduced fee of five hundred thousand dollars.
matrix.notes: The EJV is the price of a $500,000 discount on the conversion fee.

matrix.rule: Any equity joint venture created under this section shall be created for the development of a cannabis establishment, other than a cultivator, provided such equity joint venture is at least fifty per cent owned and controlled by an individual or individuals who meet, or the equity joint venture applicant is an individual who meets, the criteria established in subparagraphs (A) and (B) of subdivision (51) of section 21a-420.
matrix.notes: The ownership-AND-control language was ADDED by P.A. 22-103. Ventures formed before 24 May 2022 were formed under the earlier text.

matrix.rule: An equity joint venture applicant shall submit an application to the Social Equity Council that may include, but need not be limited to, evidence of business formation, ownership allocation, terms of ownership and financing and proof of social equity status. The equity joint venture applicant shall submit ... the organizing documents of the entity that outline the ownership stake of each backer, initial backer investment and payout information to enable the council to determine the terms of ownership.
matrix.notes: These are the records that would resolve beneficial ownership. They are held by the Social Equity Council and are not published.

matrix.rule: Upon receipt of written approval of the equity joint venture by the Social Equity Council, the equity joint venture applicant shall apply for a license from the department ... except that such application shall not be subject to the lottery process.
matrix.notes: EJVs bypass the lottery entirely. This is the mechanism by which an incumbent's affiliated ventures obtain retail licenses without a draw.

matrix.rule: Except as provided in subdivision (2) of subsection (k) of section 21a-420d, a dispensary facility, including the backers of such dispensary facility, shall not increase its ownership in an equity joint venture in excess of fifty per cent during the seven-year period after a license is issued by the department under this section.
matrix.by: P.A. 22-103; exception added by P.A. 26-8 s.71
matrix.notes: Seven years from the DEPARTMENT license date. For the Fine Fettle EJVs licensed in December 2025 that runs to December 2032.

matrix.rule: Equity joint ventures that are retailers or hybrid retailers that share a common dispensary facility backer or owner, or hybrid retailer backer or owner, shall not be located within twenty miles of each other. REPEALED. P.A. 25-101 s.17 bracketed this subsection out entirely and redesignated (g), (h) and (i) as (f), (g) and (h).
matrix.by: added P.A. 23-79 s.26; REPEALED by P.A. 25-101 s.17 (HB 6855, signed 24 June 2025)
matrix.notes: NOT CURRENT LAW ON 29 SEPTEMBER 2026. Operative 1 July 2023 to 31 December 2025 only. No later act restores it: the phrase 'twenty miles' appears zero times in P.A. 25-166, P.A. 25-168, P.A. 26-8 and P.A. 26-100. TRAP: the CGA's published chapter 420h text, fetched 29 September 2026, still prints subsection (f) and never mentions P.A. 25-101. The published revision lags the session; the acts govern.

matrix.rule: Equity joint ventures that are retailers or hybrid retailers that share a common cultivator backer or owner shall not be located within twenty miles of each other. REPEALED by P.A. 25-101 s.15, which bracketed it out and redesignated (f) as (e).
matrix.by: added P.A. 23-79 s.26; REPEALED by P.A. 25-101 s.15
matrix.notes: NOT CURRENT LAW. Same repeal date and same trap as the hybrid-retailer rule.

matrix.rule: Equity joint ventures that are retailers or hybrid retailers that share a common producer backer or owner shall not be located within twenty miles of each other. REPEALED by P.A. 25-101 s.16, which bracketed it out and redesignated (g) to (i) as (f) to (h).
matrix.by: added P.A. 23-79; REPEALED by P.A. 25-101 s.16
matrix.notes: NOT CURRENT LAW. All three parallel twenty-mile rules fell on the same day.

matrix.topic: EJV change of ownership or control — five-year gate
matrix.rule: No contract entered into or renewed on or after the effective date of this section shall provide that any change may be made in the ownership or control of any equity joint venture ... that would cause such equity joint venture not to be controlled, and at least fifty per cent owned, by an individual who meets the criteria ... unless: (A) At least five years have elapsed since a final license was issued to the equity joint venture; (B) At least ninety days before the proposed effective date of such change, the equity joint venture (i) submits a written notice to the council ... and (ii) sends a written notice to the individual ...
matrix.notes: THE EARLY EXIT. Fine Fettle and Budr asked the General Law Committee in 2025 and again in 2026 for three years. The enacted gate is FIVE years plus Council notice, stricter than either asked for. It binds contracts entered into or renewed on or after the effective date, so it is prospective only.

matrix.rule: No dispensary facility that receives approval to convert the dispensary facility's license to a hybrid-retailer license under section 21a-420t shall create more than two equity joint ventures. No such dispensary facility shall apply for, or create, any additional equity joint venture if, on July 1, 2021, such dispensary facility has created at least two equity joint ventures that have each received a provisional license.
matrix.notes: TWO per converting dispensary facility, and the cap did not exist until 24 May 2022. SURVIVES the 2025 repeal but was RENUMBERED: P.A. 25-101 s.17 redesignated subsection (h) as subsection (g) effective 1 January 2026. Cite it as 21a-420u(g) for conduct on or after that date.

matrix.topic: SEC approval of EJV ownership and control
matrix.rule: The Social Equity Council shall develop criteria for evaluating the ownership and control of any equity joint venture created under section 21a-420m, 21a-420u, 21a-420j or 21a-420aa and shall review and approve or deny in writing such equity joint venture prior to such equity joint venture being licensed ... The council shall not approve any equity joint venture applicant which shares with an equity joint venture any individual owner who meets the criteria established in subparagraphs (A) and (B) of subdivision (51) of section 21a-420, other than an individual owner in their capacity as a backer licensed under section 21a-420o.
matrix.notes: The no-shared-SEA-owner bar runs to INDIVIDUAL owners meeting the social equity criteria. An entity appearing in several ventures is not caught by this bar.

matrix.rule: Establishes what DCP may release from a license application.
matrix.notes: The project's prior work found this authorizes release of eleven items including an owner's percentage and NOTHING reaching control or any agreement bearing on it.

matrix.rule: Bars any agreement, including any consulting agreement, that transfers operational control, grants material influence regardless of whether such individual retains nominal approval rights, produces a nominal or passive owner, or impairs final decision-making authority; supplied personnel and systems are evidence of control. Annual ownership, control and financing certifications begin 15 January 2027.
matrix.notes: NOT YET IN FORCE on 29 September 2026. Cannot be applied to conduct before 1 November 2026. This is the first time Connecticut defines the control limb.

matrix.rule: A hybrid retailer shall maintain a licensed pharmacist on premises at all times when the hybrid retail location is open to the public or to qualifying patients and caregivers.
matrix.notes: This is why a multi-store operator needs multiple dispensary pharmacists.

matrix.rule: "Licensed dispensary" or "dispensary" means an individual who is a licensed pharmacist employed by a dispensary facility or hybrid retailer
matrix.notes: The credential is an individual professional registration layered on an existing pharmacist license. A licensee cannot create a pharmacist.

matrix.rule: No person may act as a dispensary or represent that such person is a licensed dispensary unless such person has obtained a license from the Commissioner of Consumer Protection pursuant to this section.
matrix.by: P.A. 12-55; amended June Sp. Sess. P.A. 21-1

matrix.rule: Would have allowed a cultivator and its backer to increase ownership above fifty per cent after three years with written Social Equity Council approval.
matrix.notes: Requested at the 19 March 2025 hearing by Derrick Gibbs (Budr) and Benjamin Zachs (Fine Fettle). Opposed by the Social Equity Council and by C-3 Ventures.
